about: gatecall's profiles, programs and national ID numbers. A company names its profiles in company-ai-policy.json ("profiles": ["default", "eu"]); profiles add up: blocked kinds, denied models and denied hosts join, a list of addresses or phone numbers counts from the lowest threshold. Every 'why' names its source.

default.about: Any company: keys and tokens, payment cards, bank accounts, personal ID numbers and lists of people's e-mail addresses or phone numbers do not leave in a prompt, a command, a web request or a tool call, and red folders are read only by a model on this computer.
default.why: The kinds a company is asked about first under card-network rules (PCI DSS), banking secrecy and data-protection law. The detectors check what can be checked - Luhn for cards, ISO 13616 mod-97 for IBANs, each country's own check digit for ID numbers - so a random number is not taken for one.

eu.about: A company in the EU: the national ID numbers of every EU country gatecall knows are stopped, not only its own country's, and a list of contacts counts from three.
eu.why: GDPR article 87 leaves the conditions for processing a national identification number to each member state, so a number from any of them is treated as one to keep inside.

us-federal-contractor.about: A US defence contractor: no AI developed by DeepSeek - not its API, not its website, not its weights on an own machine. Covered defense information (a red folder of such a company) goes only to this computer's model or to a cloud that meets the FedRAMP Moderate baseline (DFARS 252.204-7012 (b)(2)(ii)(D), https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.204-7012-safeguarding-covered-defense-information-and-cyber-incident-reporting, read 2026-10-02) - for example a GovCloud or GCC High tenant.
us-federal-contractor.why: FY2026 NDAA section 1532 (read 2026-10-02 in the Congressional Research Service summary https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF13197 and https://agora.eto.tech/instrument/2694): the Department of Defense and its contractors and subcontractors may not use covered AI - AI developed by DeepSeek, High Flyer or entities associated with High Flyer - in DoD contracts, unless the Secretary of Defense grants a case-by-case waiver. The weights on an own server are still DeepSeek's model, so a local run is stopped too.
us-federal-contractor.hosts_why: Zhipu's API (z.ai, bigmodel.cn) is closed too: Commerce added ten Zhipu entities to the Entity List on 2025-01-16 (Federal Register 2025-00704, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/16/2025-00704/addition-of-entities-to-and-revision-of-entry-on-the-entity-list), and a defence contractor keeps clear of paying a listed entity. GLM's open weights on an own machine stay allowed - no money and no data go to Zhipu (plan section 0.9).

us-dod-strict.about: For a contract that extends the rule to every AI company of a covered nation: also no models of the Chinese vendors in the price table - by their API, their website or their weights.
us-dod-strict.why: Section 1532 also bars the Department of Defense itself from using or acquiring AI from covered nations (China, Russia, Iran, North Korea) - CRS, https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF13197, read 2026-10-02. A contract can pass that wider rule on to its contractor; gatecall applies the wider list when the company names this profile.

kimi.about: Kimi's command-line agent works only in a training folder (practice files), marked by a person or listed in the company policy.
kimi.why: Kimi paid: practice files only, it has no read-only switch (opinions-late/meta-nb1.md:8, a late opinion of the plan's council; plan section 0.6, step B13).

grok.about: Grok's command-line agent works only on a cleaned copy (gatecall's copy command), never on the company's own folder.
grok.why: Grok paid: a throwaway cleaned copy and a prepaid balance (opinions-late/meta-nb1.md:8; plan section 0.6, step B13).

agy.about: Google's agy never gets a permission for everything; the text goes inside the question instead.
agy.why: agy reads a folder only after a blanket permission for all future runs; by default the text goes inside the question (opinions-late/meta-nb1.md:8; plan section 0.6, step B13).

hosts_about: Where each model API host processes data, for the company policy's deny_jurisdictions (hosts only: a model's weights on an own machine keep the data here) and deny_providers (the vendor's hosts and model names, matched like billcall's allowed_providers / deny_providers). The jurisdiction is the one billcall's price table gives for the vendor's API row, read on the vendor's own pricing or terms page on 2026-10-02; the most specific domain wins.
